summary.one_line: Bob learns that FAITH is training him to become the controlling intelligence of a Von Neumann probe, just as the candidate pool narrows to two.
summary.paragraph: Dr. Landers interrupts Bob's simulation to praise his performance under two days of subjective isolation and to discuss his temperament. In the conversation, Bob learns that two more replicant candidates have been removed from contention—one by psychotic break and one by ministerial purge—leaving only Bob and one rival. Landers then finally reveals the purpose of the project: one of them will become the controlling intelligence for a Von Neumann probe. Back in training, Bob throws himself into increasingly complex roamer coordination tasks and becomes exhilarated by the newly available project documentation and the prospect of going to the stars.
events: Dr. Landers pulls Bob out of simulation and tells him he has performed exceptionally well during two days of subjective isolation.
Bob learns that two more replicant candidates are gone, including one who suffered a psychotic break and one who was purged after Minister Travis rejected him.
After asking about Bob's tolerance for solitude, Dr. Landers reveals that the project is to create a replicant-controlled Von Neumann probe.
Bob returns to training and coordinates multiple sizes of roamers on repair and fabrication tasks.
With access to project documents at last, Bob becomes intensely excited by the possibility that he will travel to the stars.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Bob moves from impatience and guarded horror at FAITH's ruthlessness to exhilaration when he learns he might become an interstellar probe.

open_threads.text: Bob has been activated as one of five replicant candidates for a single undisclosed project, and his future depends on winning the selection.
Bob notices the roamer training room is heavily sealed and wonders why the facility needs that level of security around him and the roamers.
Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows the project is a Von Neumann probe mission, but it remains unresolved whether he or the last rival candidate will be chosen.

recent_events.text: Bob awakens in 2133 to discover he is no longer human but a replicant owned by a company in the theocratic state of FAITH.
Bob's training accelerates when he rapidly masters manipulator arms and ROAMers at the FAITH facility.
Bob learns a rival replicant has gone irretrievably insane and realizes FAITH's control extends even to his access to history and family ties.
A surprise ministerial inspection exposes FAITH's dangerous internal politics, and Bob is moved into a space-station simulation that hints at his real assignment.
Bob learns that FAITH is training him to become the controlling intelligence of a Von Neumann probe, just as the candidate pool narrows to two.
